ape_costume: I wave the ape costume at the apes. Nothing. Fur goes on, Dex. Not up.

LOOK.text: Three apes in the shallow end, scrolling phones in waterproof cases. None of them have looked up since Tuesday.

then.text: The apes look me up and down. Fur. Diamond buttons. One of them nods. 'One of us, old chap.'

else.text: I try to talk to the apes. They glance at me, then at each other. 'Not one of us, old chap.' They turn back to their phones.
Fur would help. Or a gesture of respect to whatever that giant duck is.

then.text: I try to chat. One looks up. 'Are you a member, old chap?' He goes back to his phone before I answer.

else.text: I wave at the apes. Nothing. To them, a man without fur is just weather.

PICK.text: They're in a pool. I'm not fishing for apes. I didn't bring a big enough net.

then.text: One holds up his phone. 'Check this out, old chap.' It's a sunset. 'Lovely.' 'It's my lock screen. And my plan.'

else.text: I try to say hi. The apes close ranks into a wall of wet fur. I won't get through without looking the part.

CLOSE.text: I end the conversation. 'Cheerio!' they chorus. Like a support group. Which it is.

_default: Chad looks at it. Chad yawns. 'Words, bro. Bring words.'
I hold it out. Chad squints. 'Is that a comeback? Doesn't sound like a comeback.'
Chad slides his sunglasses down, looks, slides them back up. Rejected.
pepememe: I flash the Pepe at Chad. He doesn't look. 'Show me in a duel, bro. Timing is everything.'

LOOK.text: An ape on a blue ring, sunglasses indoors, arms behind his head. That's Chad. Runs group therapy. Never lost a FUD duel.
He has never built anything. You can tell. Look how relaxed he is.

then.text: Bro. You beat me. I'm still processing. Go show the Doc.
then.speaker: Chad

else.text: Normies don't get roasted, bro. Normies get ignored.
else.speaker: Chad

else.text: Chad won't even FUD me. I need the pool to accept me first. Gerald seems to be in charge of that.

USE.text: I poke Chad's ring. He doesn't look. 'Hands are for high fives, bro. Duels are words.'

PICK.text: I can't lift Chad. 'Bro, I'm carried by my mindset. Not by you.'

PUSH.text: I nudge Chad's ring. He drifts two metres and acts like he meant it. He's good at that.

PULL.text: I pull Chad's ring closer. 'Boundaries, bro. I read a book about them. The cover.'

OPEN.text: Chad taps his head. 'Mind's already open, bro. Things fall out.'

GIVE.text: Chad doesn't take gifts. 'Gifts are for people who haven't manifested yet, bro.'

ape_costume: I hold up the ape costume. 'Fur is worn, old chap. Not brandished.'

LOOK.text: More apes in the deep end. A diamond floatie, a pink donut ring. Smiling while slowly sinking. Very British.

then.text: The deep-end apes squint at my costume. 'Fur's legit,' one says. 'Let the lad in.'

else.text: The deep-end apes glance my way. 'Who let a normie in here?' One points at the duck. 'Nobody gets in without Gerald's blessing.'

then.text: I offer one a towel. 'Dry? In this economy?' He sinks a little lower.

else.text: I reach toward them. They paddle away in perfect unison. They've practised this.

PICK.text: Wet apes. I'd lose a grip and some dignity.

then.text: 'Open your mind, old chap,' one says. 'Open the bar first,' I reply. Silence. Then: 'Fair.'

else.text: I try to get their attention. They huddle and whisper. I catch '...no fur...' and '...shoes...'. Not welcome.

CLOSE.text: 'Party's over!' I yell. They laugh nervously. One starts crying. I take it back.

_default: Gerald doesn't accept offerings like that. Gerald has standards.
I hold it out to Gerald. Gerald floats. Gerald is above all this.
The apes hiss. You don't touch Gerald with random stuff.
rubber_duck: I hold my duck up to Gerald. Then I just set it down beside him. Gently.
golden_token: I offer Gerald the golden token. Gerald doesn't do money. Gerald has a vet bill and no regrets.
water_bottle: I splash Gerald. The apes gasp. He lives in a pool. He's fine. Everyone calm down.

then.text: A giant rubber duck floatie in the pool. My rubber duck vibrates in my pocket. They can sense each other. This is either cute or terrifying.

else.text: A massive rubber duck floatie. The apes treat it with reverence. 'That's Gerald,' one whispers. 'He's been here since the ICO era.'

TALK.text: 'Gerald. Any advice?' The duck says nothing. The apes gasp. 'He only speaks to other ducks,' one whispers.

then.text: My duck and Gerald bob together. The prophecy is fulfilled. Twice would be greedy.

else.text: I place my rubber duck next to Gerald. They float side by side. The apes go silent. 'The prophecy...' one whispers. 'Two ducks...'
The apes part around me like I'm royalty. Wet, furry royalty. I think I've been accepted.
I try to ride Gerald. An ape blocks me. 'That's a sacred artifact. You need at least a rubber duck offering to approach.' A rubber duck? Where would I find one of those?

PICK.text: Gerald is too big to pick up. And the apes would riot. I've seen them with a banana.

OPEN.text: There's a valve on Gerald's belly. I could let him down. Everyone else has.

CLOSE.text: Gerald's beak is shut. Gerald does not do interviews.

glasses_3d: I watch the TV through the 3D glasses. The charts look even more 3D. ...Stop it, Dex.

LOOK.text: A TV of live charts. Green: the apes cheer. Red: they all go underwater. I'm watching too. I should stop.

TALK.text: 'Change the channel!' I yell. 'There IS no other channel,' the bartender robot replies. 'Trust me, I've tried.'

USE.text: The remote is at the bottom of the pool. 'Last chap who dove for it,' an ape warns, 'came up a different person.'

PICK.text: Bolted to the wall. Adrian bolts everything. Except himself, apparently.

OPEN.text: I open the TV menu. Options: 'CHARTS' and 'MORE CHARTS'. I close it before I pick one.

CLOSE.text: I reach for the off button. 'NO!' scream all the apes at once. I step back slowly.

LOOK.text: A well-stocked bar. A robot bartender polishes a glass that's already spotless. It's been polishing it for a while.

TALK.text: I approach the bar. The robot looks up. 'What'll it be? We have everything except real financial returns.'

USE.text: The robot slides me a green drink. 'On the house. The Liquidation.' It tastes like lime and bad decisions.

PICK.text: I reach for a bottle. The robot takes it back before my hand arrives. Faster than me. Faster than anyone.

OPEN.text: I open a bottle. Fizz. 'That is the house IPA,' the robot says. 'It tastes different every time. That is a defect.'

CLOSE.text: I put the cap back on. 'Thank you,' says the robot. 'Nobody here closes anything.'

_default: The bartender scans it. 'Not on the menu.' Fair.
'I do not accept that as payment.' The robot is very polite about it.
The robot beeps. 'Tips only.' That isn't a tip.
golden_token: I slide the golden token across. The robot slides it back. 'Coins are not tips. Tips are not coins. I checked.'
energy_drink: I offer the bartender my energy drink. 'I do not drink. I am the drinks.'

LOOK.text: A chrome robot in a bowtie. Nametag: 'B.O.T. — Beverage Operations Terminal'. Scratched below: 'formerly: Trading Bot v2.3'.

else.speaker: B.O.T.
else.text: *scans face* Identity: UNKNOWN. Species: HUMAN. Access level: NONE.

else.speaker: B.O.T.
else.text: This bar serves apes only. Come back when you look the part. Dress code is strictly enforced.
The robot's LED eyes flash red briefly. Clearly, I need to blend in if I want to get served here.

then.text: I reach for its control panel. 'Buy me a drink first,' it says. I can't. It's the one with the drinks.

else.speaker: B.O.T.
else.text: *arm blocks access* Apes only. No exceptions. I don't make the rules. I just enforce them. Mechanically.

PICK.text: It weighs 200 kilos and has a taser arm. I'll pick something smaller. Like a fight with Chad.

OPEN.text: I open its chest panel. Inside: a tiny hamster wheel. 'Backup generator,' it says, closing it. 'Do not ask about the hamster.'

CLOSE.text: 'Please do not switch me off. Last time, I rebooted and served everyone milk.'

LOOK.text: Banana peels all around the pool edge. Either messy guests or performance art. With apes, it's both.

TALK.text: I talk to a banana peel. Of all my witnesses, it's the most forthcoming.

USE.text: I step on a peel on purpose. Classic. The apes score it: '7, mate. Weak landing.'

PICK.text: I pick up a peel. An ape glares. 'That's my spot, mate.' I put it back exactly where it was.

OPEN.text: It's already open. That's what a peel is. A banana's closing argument.

CLOSE.text: I try to put the banana back together. The apes watch, fascinated. Nobody helps.

LOOK.text: A junk pile by the stairs: empty cans, torn whitepapers, a cracked phone. Something in there might be worth digging for.

TALK.text: 'What are you hiding?' A can falls off the top. It's either a sign or gravity. Gravity, Dex.

USE.text: I rummage through the junk. My hand comes out sticky and wiser.

then.text: Nothing else worth digging for. Unless I want the cracked phone. I don't.

else.text: I dig through the pile and push aside some crumpled whitepapers and an alarming number of banana peels. Wait. There's a rubber duck in here? How did this survive the carnage?
It squeaks when I pick it up. The apes look up from their phones. 'Is that... a duck?' one whispers reverently. 'Gerald will want to meet it.'

OPEN.text: A crumpled to-do list: '1. Swim. 2. Bananas. 3. Swim.' Somebody here has life figured out.

CLOSE.text: I push the trash back into a pile. An ape nods. 'Tidy, old chap.' He throws a peel on it.

keycard: No card reader. Ominous doors run on vibes.

then.text: The door to the MemeLAB. Now I know what's inside, the warning sign looks modest.

else.text: A heavy metal door, pitch black behind the gap. A sign: 'AUTHORIZED WHALES ONLY'. Underneath, scratched: 'and Gerald'.
I reach for the handle. A cold draft pushes back. The air smells like... memes? Digital decay? Something glows faintly behind the door.
I push harder. The door groans open. Red and blue light spills out. What the hell is in there?
I try the door. It resists, then yields with a metallic shriek. Red and cyan light pours through the crack.
Whatever's in there has been sealed for a while. Only one way to find out...

TALK.text: I knock. Something knocks back. Three times. Like a three-factor door. I back away slowly.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a door. I can barely pick up hints.

CLOSE.text: Already closed. Good. Doors with that much attitude should stay closed.

else.text: I push the door. It groans open. Red and blue light floods out — like stepping into a glitched dimension.
I pull the door. Cold air hits my face. But this time I see it — red and cyan light from inside. A lab.

LOOK.text: Stairs back up to the clinic reception. Dry land. Forms. Nurse Gwei.

TALK.text: The stairs creak like they're disappointed in me. Penny does that face too.

PICK.text: I can't pick up stairs. I checked last time too.

CLOSE.text: No door to close. The apes' singing follows me up the stairs.

LOOK.text: 'The Art of the Rug'. Author: Anonymous. Foreword by 'a whale who wishes to remain unnamed'. Riveting.
A bookmark at chapter 3. Somebody here does homework. Suspicious.

TALK.text: 'Has anyone read this?' An ape scoffs. 'Read it, mate? I'm chapter seven.'

USE.text: Chapter 1: 'Buy High'. Chapter 2: 'Sell Low'. Chapter 3: 'How to Win a FUD Duel'. Finally, something useful.
One line, underlined twice: 'Comebacks are learned at the shallow end, the deep end, and the bar.'
Three sources. A real detective checks all three. Even the wet one.

PICK.text: Heavier than it looks. Pages stiff with pool water and what I hope is highlighter. I put it back.

OPEN.text: Chapter 1: 'Buy High'. Chapter 2: 'Sell Low'. Chapter 3: 'How to Win a FUD Duel'. Finally, something useful.
One line, underlined twice: 'Comebacks are learned at the shallow end, the deep end, and the bar.'
Three sources. A real detective checks all three. Even the wet one.

CLOSE.text: I close the book. A bookmark falls out: a receipt for $SAFU. The bookmark taught the class.

LOOK.text: A soggy blue notebook: 'MY TRADING JOURNAL — Day 1 to Lambo'. 'Lambo' is crossed out. Then 'Ramen'. Then 'Toast'.

TALK.text: 'Whose journal is this?' Three apes raise a hand. Then they look at each other. Then they put them down.

USE.text: Today's entry is one word, forty-seven times. The handwriting gets worse each line. The last one is in crayon.

PICK.text: Pages fall out like leaves. 'Zoom out.' 'Still early.' 'Fine.' I put them back in a different order. Nobody will notice.

OPEN.text: A folded chart in the back pocket. 'Bought here.' 'And here.' 'Why did I buy here.' 'I need help.' Same handwriting as mine. Spooky.

CLOSE.text: The last page: 'Don't feel sorry for me. I'm in a pool now. Living my best life.' The ink is smudged. Pool water. Probably.

intro.speaker: Chad
intro.text: New guy wants to duel? Rules: I FUD, you reply. Miss once and I win. Ready, bro?

choices.text: The Doc says you respect holders.
What do I get if I win?

vip_round.speaker: Chad
vip_round.text: A holder? Respect, bro. We skip the warm-up. Final round, right now.

prize.speaker: Chad
prize.text: My sobriety token. The Doc collects them. Nobody's ever taken mine.

i3.speaker: Chad
i3.text: You bought the top so hard, they named it after you.

choices.text: I can tell. They left the receipts floating in the pool.
Then today they'll hear you lose.
A broken clock is right twice a day. You're on a streak of zero.
And you sold the bottom so often, they gave you a loyalty card.

i1.speaker: Chad
i1.text: Your bags are so heavy, the lifeguard filed a complaint.

choices.text: A broken clock is right twice a day. You're on a streak of zero.
Still more detail than your exit plan.
At least mine float. Yours sank in a kiddie pool.
Then today they'll hear you lose.

i5.speaker: Chad
i5.text: Your roadmap is a napkin with a frowny face on it.

choices.text: Still more detail than your exit plan.
And you sold the bottom so often, they gave you a loyalty card.
At least mine float. Yours sank in a kiddie pool.
I can tell. They left the receipts floating in the pool.

i7.speaker: Chad
i7.text: Name ONE thing you've built that anyone still wants.

choices.text: I can tell. They left the receipts floating in the pool.
Then today they'll hear you lose.
A broken clock is right twice a day. You're on a streak of zero.

win.speaker: Chad
win.text: Fine. You win. Take it. A sobriety token. Worth nothing. That's the point.

win_2.speaker: Chad
win_2.text: Show the Doc. He collects these.

win_dex.text: I beat Chad at FUD. With a frog. My mum would not understand, and that's fine.

lose.speaker: Chad
lose.text: HA! Weak, bro. Chad wins. Chad always wins.

h_left.speaker: Chad
h_left.text: Even the posh apes in the shallow end have better comebacks, bro.

h_right.speaker: Chad
h_right.text: The deep end roasts harder than you, and they're mostly underwater.

h_bar.speaker: Chad
h_bar.text: Even the bartender has better lines. And he's a toaster.

h_pepe.speaker: Chad
h_pepe.text: Nobody down here ever MADE anything, bro. That's why I'm undefeated.

h_any.speaker: Chad
h_any.text: Every FUD has one right comeback. You keep picking the wrong one. Respect, actually.

lose_end.speaker: Chad
lose_end.text: Run it back whenever, bro. Losing is free. Winning costs a personality.

bye.speaker: Chad
bye.text: Smart. Fear is the first step to sobriety.

greeting.speaker: Shallow-End Ape
greeting.text: Ah, a new chap. Fancy a spot of FUD? We duel every Tuesday. It's always Tuesday down here.

why.speaker: Shallow-End Ape
why.text: Deep end's for leverage, old boy. We're spot traders. We like to touch the bottom.

d1.speaker: Shallow-End Ape
d1.text: Your bags are so heavy, the lifeguard filed a complaint, old chap.

d1_r.speaker: Other Shallow-End Ape
d1_r.text: At least mine float. Yours sank in a kiddie pool.

d2.speaker: Shallow-End Ape
d2.text: I've seen better hands on a broken clock.

d2_dex.text: Your face is a broken clock.

d2_r.speaker: Other Shallow-End Ape
d2_r.text: A broken clock is right twice a day. You're on a streak of zero.

d_end.speaker: Shallow-End Ape
d_end.text: Two-nil, old chap. Do write those down.

d_end_dex.text: Written down. In my phone. Right next to my losses.

greeting.speaker: Deep-End Ape
greeting.text: Gerald's friend! Welcome to the deep end, bro. Down here we roast. Wanna get roasted?

choices.text: Who's the guy on the diamond floatie?

chad.speaker: Deep-End Ape
chad.text: That's Chad. He runs group. Undefeated at FUD. Don't let him smell fear. He can smell fear.

d3.speaker: Deep-End Ape
d3.text: You bought the top so hard, they named it after you, bro.

d3_r.speaker: Diamond-Floatie Ape
d3_r.text: And you sold the bottom so often, they gave you a loyalty card.

d4.speaker: Deep-End Ape
d4.text: Nobody in this pool has ever heard of you.

d4_r.speaker: Diamond-Floatie Ape
d4_r.text: Then today they'll hear you lose.

d_end.speaker: Deep-End Ape
d_end.text: Brutal. You lost to the comebacks, bro. Steal them. Everyone does.

greeting.speaker: B.O.T.
greeting.text: Welcome to the Liquidity Pool. I'm B.O.T. — Beverage Operations Terminal. Formerly a high-frequency trading algorithm. Now I mix drinks and watch apes provide liquidity. With their bodies. It's... a lateral move.

what_is_this.speaker: B.O.T.
what_is_this.text: Dr. Satoshi's experimental DeFi therapy. Literal liquidity provision. The apes believe being IN the pool makes them liquidity providers. The green water is infused with 'decentralized minerals'. It's just food coloring. But the APY on their delusions is remarkable.

therapy_works.speaker: B.O.T.
therapy_works.text: Define 'work'. They haven't checked their portfolios in 45 minutes. That's a clinic record. One of them even made eye contact with another human yesterday. Baby steps.

patients.speaker: B.O.T.
patients.text: Chronic cases, all of them. That one bought the top of every cycle since 2017. That one over there? Mortgaged his house for a dog coin. And the one with the diamond floatie? He's actually profitable. He just comes for the vibes.

profitable.speaker: B.O.T.
profitable.text: Survivor's guilt. He made money while his friends got liquidated. Now he floats here, pretending to be broke. It's the crypto version of a support group. 'Hi, I'm Chad, and I sold the top.' *gasps from the pool*

patient_zero.speaker: B.O.T.
patient_zero.text: Patient Zero... *servos whir* My data logs show someone matching that description. They were here before the pool was a pool. When this was still a server room. They left something behind — a message in my memory banks I can't delete.

message.speaker: B.O.T.
message.text: 'The cure isn't in the code. It's in the community.' That's all. Encrypted with a key I don't have. Whoever Patient Zero was, they understood something the rest of us are still trying to compute.

when.speaker: B.O.T.
when.text: Block 1. Not block 1 of Base. Block 1 of this building. Before AdrianLAB was AdrianLAB. Before the trading floors and the diamond protocol. When it was just... someone's dream in a basement. Like all the best things.

drink.speaker: B.O.T.
drink.text: The house special: 'The Liquidation'. It's green, it burns, and you'll question your life choices afterward. Just like real trading. Cheers.

farewell.speaker: B.O.T.
farewell.text: Come back anytime. The pool is always open. The bar is always stocked. And the charts... the charts never sleep. Neither do I. Because I'm a robot. That was the joke. I'll work on my delivery.

lesson.speaker: B.O.T.
lesson.text: House rule: every Liquidation comes with a FUD lesson. Defend yourself.

r5.speaker: B.O.T.
r5.text: FUD sample one. Your roadmap is a napkin with a frowny face on it.

r5_ok.speaker: B.O.T.
r5_ok.text: Insufficient. Correct output: 'Still more detail than your exit plan.'

r6.speaker: B.O.T.
r6.text: I've been liquidated by better people than you.

r6_ok.speaker: B.O.T.
r6_ok.text: Correct output: 'I can tell. They left the receipts floating in the pool.'

r_tip.speaker: B.O.T.
r_tip.text: Free tip, as a former trading bot. Chad has one weakness: he has never made anything.

script.text: I hold up the rare Pepe to B.O.T.

script.speaker: B.O.T.
script.text: Is that... a rare Pepe? FROM the MemeLAB? My circuits haven't processed meme alpha like this since the great Doge pump of 2021.

script.speaker: B.O.T.
script.text: The patients here were trying to ENGINEER viral memes. Turn them into tokenized assets. 'Meme as a Service' — MaaS. Dr. Satoshi shut it down when the memes became... sentient.
B.O.T.'s eyes flash green. For a moment, every screen in the pool bar displays the same Pepe face.

script.speaker: B.O.T.
script.text: You've seen behind the veil. The MemeLAB was their crown jewel. Keep that Pepe safe — it's the last proof of what they were building down there.
MEME ACHIEVEMENT — Decoded the MemeLAB conspiracy
I show the rare Pepe to the apes floating in the pool.
They all turn simultaneously. One of them gasps. Another starts crying. A third whispers reverently: 'It's... the original. The specimen from the lab.'
They stare at the Pepe with a mixture of awe and PTSD. These apes have seen things.
I flash the Pepe at the right side of the pool.
An ape does a spit-take with his green drink. 'WHERE did you get that?! That's from behind the door! How did you survive the anaglyph?!'
'3D glasses,' I say. The ape stares at me like I've just explained quantum physics to a goldfish.
I hold the Pepe next to the giant rubber duck. They stare at each other. Two icons. Two legends. One pool.
For a brief, beautiful moment, I feel like I'm holding the entire internet in my hands.
